You are revising the BookMinder project-memory skill under a ruling the author just made. Work in /home/user/BookMinder on the current branch. Read this brief fully before touching anything.

## The ruling (author's decisions, this session; paraphrased unless quoted)

1. The skill page `.claude/skills/bookminder/references/apple-books-domain.md` currently (v2.2, commit 2f28017) replaces facts with pointers to `docs/apple_books.md` sections. Author: that "defeats the purpose of the skill because it basically requires that doc to be fully present in context to make sense of this skill's section. We need to invert it. This skill must encode compressed learned facts and reference doc's sections for more details where needed." The previous revision v2.1 (`git show 2f28017^:.claude/skills/bookminder/references/apple-books-domain.md`) had the facts but also "accidental complexity from the way how we discovered those details" — discovery narrative, per-title anecdotes, row counts, chronology, line numbers. v3 = v2.1's facts at v2.2's economy.
2. No verification stamps anywhere (no `verified@tree` / `observed-2025` / `hypothesis`, no legend). Author: stamping every entry is "extremely distracting" and is provenance in another costume. The only distinction that survives is known versus unknown. Unknowns are stated as facts about ignorance ("ZSTATE 5 is unmapped", "Want to Read ordering is unknown", "whether the database carries a usable path column was never checked"). Author on this: "facts about ignorance—yep, excellent!"
3. No environment sentences. Delete "This environment has no live Apple Books database…" and, in repo-geography B-29, "This cloud environment has no live Apple Books library, so any exploration here runs against fixtures only: say so explicitly and mark conclusions provisional." A portable skill never states which machine it is running on.
4. The router invariant "Apple Books schema claims are hypotheses until re-verified against a live database; re-take the census, never recall it" is WRONG as a standing rule and goes. Author's reasoning: the integration suite is the verification instrument; fixtures are exact vertical slices copied from a real database with `copy_book_to_fixture.sh`, correct by construction; specs pin the assumptions; a green suite IS the verification; re-establishing schema facts in an agent session is "pure waste". The live database is an escalation target with a specific trigger: reality disagrees with the fixtures (a real library breaks what the suite says works, or a new Apple Books / macOS release lands), or a story needs a state the fixtures do not hold (then the author adjusts a real book and it gets copied in). Replacement invariant, shape for you to draft in one or two lines: schema truth lives in the specs — what a spec pins against the fixtures is established; a claim no spec pins is exploration residue, not knowledge; go to a live library only on drift or when a needed state is missing from the fixtures.
5. "Enumerate all distinct values DB-first and characterize each, never reason UI-first from values already seen" was the author's 2025 exploration METHOD. It stays as one line of method for when exploration does happen (in the ZSTATE entry and in the recon brief), not as a per-session reflex and not as a "signature reflex" heading.
6. Entries: call the numbered items "entries" (B-43 is entry B-43). Author: "don't constrain yourself during the rewrite with holding the identifiers stable" — he suspects the entry count was reduced too much earlier; split or merge as the content demands and do "a consistent renumbering pass". Keep the `B-` prefix. Where an existing entry survives unchanged in scope, prefer keeping its id; record every id change (old → new, split, merged, retired) in the footer roster of `.coordination/compile/rule-index-bookminder.md` and update every cross-reference inside `.claude/skills/bookminder/` (router page map, other pages) so nothing dangles.
7. `docs/apple_books.md` is NOT to be edited. It is the territory map from the 2025 research spike, with evidence and screenshots; the skill points into it by SECTION NAME (never line numbers) only where depth or evidence lives beyond the fact itself.
8. Evergreen: no timestamps, no ratification stamps, no "as of", no transient recovery language, no harness facts, never mention CLAUDE.md, no line numbers (file names only), no size figures, no counts that rot. Never hard-wrap prose: one line per paragraph or bullet.

## Deliverables, in order, each committed by you as it lands (stage files explicitly by name, never `git add .`/`-A`; commit messages explain why, referencing the ruling; end every commit message with the two trailer lines below; do NOT push)

Trailer lines:
```
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01233T9ME4hRqtMsmEqbGtbP
```

**D1 — `.claude/skills/bookminder/references/apple-books-domain.md` v3.** Sources for facts: v2.1 (git show above), v2.2 (current file), `docs/apple_books.md` (read it whole once), and the code: read `bookminder/apple_books/library.py` and `specs/apple_books/library_spec.py` + `specs/apple_books/library_integration_spec.py` whole, and verify every code-encoded fact you state (glob discovery, APPLE_EPOCH, is_sample/is_cloud predicates, the cloud-filter predicate, plist list-shape guard, path="" placeholder, the two container paths) against them — a fact you could not verify in the tree is stated as what the record says, never as what the code does. Every entry: the fact, why it matters to BookMinder code or specs (one clause), and where depth lives if anywhere (doc section name, or a file name). Sections: keep a sensible grouping (data sources / the library table and its columns / environment / working the database / the doc's standing); drop "signature reflex" framing. One-paragraph intro stating what the page is and its relation to the doc; no stamp legend. Retain, in fact form: the two containers and glob trap; plist-vs-database roles incl. plist incompleteness, `updateDate` meaning unknown (the `sort_by='updated'` YAGNI deletion is the consequence worth one clause), never filter by on-disk file existence; Apple epoch; ZSTATE 1/3/6 mapping, 5 unmapped, the exploration method line; composite sample predicate, ZISSAMPLE=0 proves nothing, lifecycle proposed-not-observed, per-title values are point-in-time; display-vs-filter cloud divergence and the revert governance (change neither side without the author's direction and a spec); ZCONTENTTYPE mapping unverified; ZTITLE not a key (the doc's screenshot beside that claim is the evidence); ZISFINISHED=1 alone means finished; ZLASTOPENDATE never observed NULL with progress>0, so unguarded; samples never observed with progress and position tracked in AEAnnotation, both second-hand; list recent's progress>0 filter makes sample listing belong on list all; Want to Read computed not marked, composition observed, ordering unknown; container lifecycle facts and the sudo requirement; plist list-of-dicts shape, plistlib not plutil, swift rendering for exploration; path correlation open, path column never checked; query discipline (sqlite3 CLI, no throwaway scripts, targeted columns, `?` placeholders, ASCII-prefix LIKE retry, IN batching); the doc's standing and the author's doc-editing rules (descriptive of storage, no prescriptive SQL, all SQL in the single Database-to-UI-Mapping section, UI quirks documented never replicated, screenshots committed beside claims and platform-labelled, preserve segmentation). Aim for the shortest text that still lets an agent write correct code without opening the doc.

**D2 — `.coordination/apple-books-recon.md`.** The meta-task brief for the Apple Books drift reconnaissance on the author's local machines. Base it on the plan recorded at `.coordination/threads.md` line 71 (read that line) — read-only census on both machines (Mac mini current macOS, Intel MacBook older macOS; iCloud syncs one library across both), app + OS versions, Z_METADATA / Z_MODELCACHE schema fingerprint (the fixture DB carries only ZBKLIBRARYASSET and user_version 0, so no version metadata was ever captured), `.schema` diff against the fixture, fresh ZSTATE census, row counts; then the doc update pass consumes it; a version-handling strategy only if drift is measured. Add the VERIFICATION CHECKLIST keyed by v3 entry id: every unknown or unpinned claim the skill page states as ignorance or as record-only (ZSTATE 5; the cross-device disagreement — cloud-icon books seen at ZSTATE 1/3/6 vs the doc mapping 1 as local, iPhone UI vs Mac database; ZCONTENTTYPE; ZLASTOPENDATE nulls; sample progress and AEAnnotation position; Want to Read ordering; path column; ZSTATE-1 semantics), plus the doc claims that had no recorded correction and await live re-verification — take those from the "NO-EDIT (16)" and "Doc vs skill disagreement" sections of `.coordination/compile/apple-books-doc-repair-evidence.md` (read it), rewritten as checklist items, not copied. Each item: what to check, the query or command shape if known, which entry or doc section it updates. No wide tables — bullets. The evidence file itself stays; do not delete it.

**D3 — Defect sweep of `.claude/skills/bookminder/references/repo-geography-and-fixtures.md` and `.claude/skills/bookminder/references/current-state-and-open-decisions.md`.** Same defect class only: remove environment sentences, every `(verified@tree …)`/stamp, every line-number reference (keep file names), size figures ("~12M", "~2.5M", "~240K" — say "large" or drop), rot-prone counts; convert any pointer-without-fact to fact-with-pointer. Do not restructure or renumber these pages beyond what cross-references to renumbered domain entries require; do not touch `goals-and-history.md` (already approved) except to fix a dangling cross-reference if one exists.

**D4 — `.claude/skills/bookminder/SKILL.md`.** Replace the retired invariant with the new one (item 4). Re-derive the page-map line for the domain page from v3's actual contents (it currently advertises verification status, the census reflex, and the doc's epistemic status). Touch nothing else in the router.

**D5 — `.coordination/compile/rule-index-bookminder.md`.** Footer roster: record the id mapping from item 6.

## Constraints
- Touch no tracked file other than the deliverables named above.
- Never read anything under `claude-dev-log-diary/`.
- Run `python3 .claude/skills/skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py .claude/skills/bookminder` if that script exists, before the final commit, and report its result.
- Before committing each deliverable, grep your output for: `verified@`, `observed-2025`, `hypothesis)`, `:[0-9]+` after a `.py`/`.sh`/`.toml` file name, `CLAUDE.md`, `2025-`/`2026-` dates, "this environment", "cloud". Report the grep as clean or list what remains and why.

## Return
A maximum-12-line summary: commits made (hash + one clause each), word count of v3 vs v2.2, the id mapping in one line, validator result, grep result, and anything you deviated from in this brief with the reason.

## Orientation

- **B-20 — Cheapest grounding.** `/hi` (and this skill) already supply the session-start census — read what you were given before running discovery commands of your own; re-deriving project structure by hand is what the author interrupts. The production package is tiny (`bookminder/cli.py` + `bookminder/apple_books/library.py`) — read it whole before any task; it is cheaper than guessing, and its current size is one `wc -l` away, never a remembered number. The behavior spec of the whole system is `pytest --spec`. Feature entry chain: `bookminder/cli.py` → `bookminder/apple_books/library.py`; everything else is docs, fixtures, or process. Never run unfiltered `find .` or repo-wide line counts — both this repo and BookMind keep a vendored venv in-tree, and the two raw line counts that once produced a "44% code reduction" headline were almost entirely site-packages; exclude caches, any vendored venv, and `claude-dev-log-diary/` from every listing or metric.
- **B-21 — Land mines.** `claude-dev-log-diary/` (~12M of hand-curated session transcripts) is permission-gated: never read, grep, commit, or surface it — including indirectly via `git diff`/`git show`/`git log -p` — without explicit user consent, and a grant is scoped to the exact excerpt and manner named (range reads of the named lines, not whole-file ingests — one whole-file read against an explicit line-range grant wasted 10% of context and drew a rebuke; and never from a background subagent, where the author cannot see or stop what is being read — he kills those on sight). One day-file may contain several sessions (`^claude` marks each start) and only the session-end cost figure is valid. `docs/ui/apple/` holds ~2.5M of binary screenshots — reference by path, never Read. `specs/apple_books/fixtures/All_Books*.swift` (~240K each) are grep-only and deliberately untracked pending curation — do not gitignore them and never stage them. Fixture `.sqlite` files are binary — query with `sqlite3`, never Read. The `./xs` symlink resolves into the forbidden diary directory: execute it as the documented tool, do not read it as a file. Zero-byte fixture files (`401429854.epub`, corrupted_db_user's plist+sqlite) are intentional — that is the fixture's point, not damage to repair.
- **B-22 — Spec tree layout.** Specs are concern-based at HEAD: `specs/cli_spec.py`, `specs/cli_formatting_spec.py`, `specs/apple_books/library_spec.py`, `specs/apple_books/library_integration_spec.py`, with fixtures co-located under `specs/apple_books/fixtures/`. Coverage caveat: `specs/cli_spec.py` drives the CLI via `subprocess` (`sys.executable -m bookminder`, cli_spec.py:19-38), and pytest-cov does not follow child processes — never read a coverage gap in subprocess-exercised code as evidence it is untested.

## Session-transcript preservation

- **B-32 — Native transcript backup (cloud/ephemeral containers only).** `claude-dev-log-diary/jsonl/` preserves full session transcripts in the agentic system's native format — the machine-readable source the day-files only shadow; layout and copy commands live in its README. When working in an ephemeral container (Claude Code cloud infra), the container's transcript dies with it, so snapshot the session's `.jsonl` file + directory from the harness project store (`/root/.claude/projects/<project>/`) into `jsonl/cloud-<year>/` and commit: (1) always toward session end, when the final branch push is being prepared; (2) incrementally at natural stable points — after a major phase of work lands, or when resuming after a long pause (the pause's tail is then on disk). Copies are append-only extensions, so re-snapshotting is always safe; batch the snapshot into an adjacent commit rather than making high-frequency snapshot-only commits. A transcript cannot contain its own final minutes — the true tail of a session is captured by the next session's first snapshot. Local (non-ephemeral) sessions are exempt: the harness store persists there, and the author owns backup timing.

## Backlog and stories

- **B-23 — Backlog practice.** Stories are YAML cards under `stories/` in story-map columns: `discover` covers listing, filtering, admin access, and error handling; `access` is controlling the Apple Books app; `review` is highlights and notes; `export` is text extraction. Every card carries a mandatory `status` from the vocabulary the instruction layer's backlog rules define — status only, no priority/assignee metadata (YAGNI). TODO.md's Discover Column is a bare list of story paths in implementation order: the order is the plan, so take the next story in order rather than offering a menu, and keep the list free of emoji, numbering, and per-item rationale. Completed Features is an immutable record of the journey — never reorder or remove entries; annotate a reopened story in place (`[REOPENED: ...]`); refactorings are not listed there (user-visible stories only); a doc deletion gets a one-line breadcrumb with its commit hash. Parked backlog items must carry enough of the HOW (mechanism, trigger, expected behavior) that a fresh session can execute them without asking.

## Settled design decisions in the code

- **B-24 — CLI shape.** `main` is a Click group; `list` is a subgroup declared `@main.group(name="list")` on a function named `list_cmd` — never name the function `list`, which shadows the builtin and breaks `list[Book]` annotations at import time (fix name collisions at the source, not with deprecated typing aliases). Subcommands `recent` and `all` share options via the `with_common_list_options` decorator (Click does not inherit group options). Filter vocabulary: one `--filter` option (single value at HEAD — multiple filters are deferred future work with no story yet) whose values are attribute names with `!` negation — `cloud`/`!cloud` and `sample`/`!sample` implemented today, with reading status (`finished`, `unread`, `in-progress`) already assigned to the same option by the approved plan; there is no `--flag`, no `--status`, and no `--type` — those were considered and reversed, so reintroducing one is reopening a settled decision, not a design choice. `!` and not `-` because Click parses a leading `-` as an option; filters are orthogonal to list commands (nothing in Apple Books' UI makes them command-specific). `list recent` deliberately replicates Apple's Continue section so that an agent consuming the future MCP surface and the human looking at the app share one frame of reference. `--user` is simultaneously a real admin feature (examine another user's books) and the test seam — the admin use case is what licenses it in production. The CLI owns no domain knowledge: it passes the raw `--user` string and filter through to the library and delegates path resolution and querying there.
- **B-25 — The Book type.** One `Book` TypedDict with `NotRequired` optional fields; never a parallel type for a variant that adds a field. Only `title` and `author` are required; `path` and `updated` are `NotRequired` — the type guarantees only what every code path can honestly supply, and the DB-backed path fabricates `path` as `""` (see the domain page's open path-correlation problem). TypedDict is a static annotation only: it produces a plain dict, no attribute access, no runtime key enforcement.

## Fixture architecture

- **B-26 — Synthetic $HOME personas and the front-door seam.** Integration fixtures are synthetic home-directory trees under `specs/apple_books/fixtures/users/<persona>/` replicating Apple's container layout path-for-path. Each persona encodes a container state observed on a real machine: `test_reader` (full library), `fresh_books_user` (all containers, empty plist, empty-schema sqlite), `legacy_books_user` (containers but no BKLibrary directory), `never_opened_user` (only the OS-created `com.apple.iBooksX` container, holding an empty `BKLibrary` directory and nothing else — no BKAgentService, no plist, no sqlite), `corrupted_db_user` (zero-byte plist and sqlite; note a corruption scenario needs the full container present or the plist check fires before the sqlite error). The legacy/never-opened split exists to exercise two distinct error paths (verified@tree, library.py:26-37): a missing `BKLibrary` directory raises "BKLibrary directory not found", an empty one raises "No BKLibrary database found in:" — which is why `never_opened_user`'s empty directory is load-bearing and kept tracked by its leaf `.gitkeep`. The seam is the front door: `--user` with an absolute path is used verbatim as the home directory, a bare name resolves to `/Users/<name>`, `None` to `Path.home()` — exactly three cases, specced in `library._get_user_path`, no falsy-string case. Specs must pass absolute fixture paths (a relative path is treated as a username and silently rewritten). This seam exists because fixtures through the product's own parameter exercise the real path-construction code, where patching a private module name would bypass it; the older module-constant seam (`BKLIBRARY_DB_FILE`-style) survives only with its known limitation — it is an in-process substitution resolved at import time and cannot cross a subprocess boundary.
- **B-27 — Fixture data discipline.** The fixture database carries the real schema verbatim — dump `.schema ZBKLIBRARYASSET` from a live database, never hand-write a schema. Rows are copies of real, complete book records: populate only with `specs/apple_books/fixtures/copy_book_to_fixture.sh` (ATTACH DATABASE + explicit column list minus Z_PK, generated from `PRAGMA table_info`), never hand-written or hand-edited SQL — an invented or edited row encodes the agent's beliefs exactly where the spec is supposed to be falsifiable. If a needed state does not exist, the author adjusts a real book in his library and it gets copied. Use the existing scripts (`create_fixture.sh` creates, `copy_book_to_fixture.sh` populates); if a script fails, debug the script. Scripts never delete — cleanup is a deliberate human act. Script rules: parameter variable is `FIXTURE_USER`, never `USERNAME` (a zsh special parameter that silently shadows the argument — this bug is fixed at HEAD, copy_book_to_fixture.sh:8); SQL-escape titles by doubling quotes; locate the fixture DB by the same `BKLibrary-*.sqlite` glob production uses; root every path at PROJECT_ROOT and verify the resolved path before the first write (a swapped path once planted a stray fixture inside the real Apple Books directory). Document how each fixture was derived in `docs/test_fixtures.md` in the same commit. Preserve intentionally-empty directories with a single `.gitkeep` at the leaf. Prefer extending `test_reader` over new personas unless a test needs isolation. After any fixture change, verify through the product: `python -m bookminder list recent --user <absolute fixture path>`.
- **B-28 — Fixture census freshness.** Never rely on a remembered census of what `test_reader` contains — earlier remembered censuses went stale when books were swapped. The census truth is one query away: `sqlite3 "specs/apple_books/fixtures/users/test_reader/Library/Containers/com.apple.iBooksX/Data/Documents/BKLibrary/BKLibrary-fixture.sqlite" "SELECT ZTITLE, ZSTATE, ZISSAMPLE, ZREADINGPROGRESS FROM ZBKLIBRARYASSET"`. Lore: the zero-byte `401429854.epub` placeholder is "Growing Object-Oriented Software, Guided by Tests" — the project's canonical known book, named in ORIGINAL_VISION.md.
- **B-29 — Real DB vs fixtures.** Exploration of Apple Books behavior runs read-only against a real database — fixtures can only confirm what was built into them; when reality shows a new case worth capturing, it gets copied into the fixture. This cloud environment has no live Apple Books library, so any exploration here runs against fixtures only: say so explicitly and mark conclusions provisional. Fixtures freeze time — any recency-window behavior must be specified with controlled time, or the snapshot silently ages out of the window.
- **B-30 — Toolchain and environment.** Python pinned `==3.13.*` (pyproject.toml:11) — pinning, not a permissive floor, because reproducibility across machines depends on one interpreter; uv + ruff + mypy, setuptools backend; ruff `target-version = "py312"` (pyproject.toml:71) stays until the pinned ruff accepts py313. Run tests from the venv: `source .venv/bin/activate && pytest` (`uvx bookminder` fails — unpublished; bare `uv run` re-downloads CPython). The cloud environment may arrive with no `.venv` — provision with `uv venv && uv pip install -e ".[dev]"`. When ruff disagrees between shell and hook, compare `.pre-commit-config.yaml`'s pinned `rev:` against `ruff --version` in the venv. `check-toml` stays in pre-commit — an invalid pyproject once passed an all-green run and broke the second machine.
- **B-31 — Repo maintenance principles.** Exactly one source of truth per concern; a migration deletes the superseded file inside itself. Never invent identity metadata — the author is Pavol Vaskovic (pali@pali.sk); ask or leave blank. An untested causal claim does not go into docs: if you assert X is required, remove X and show the failure first, and never document a command until you have run it and shown it working. Judge any document by whether it is referred back to and changes behavior on this project — retrospective meta-analysis docs fail both tests and the author calls them slop. README bash snippets carry no inline comments (readers copy-paste them); explanation goes in the prose above.

# Current state and open decisions

State claims rot. This page names where truth lives and which decisions are genuinely open; when it conflicts with the tree, the tree wins — then update this page.

## Where truth lives

- **B-60 — Read state, don't recall it.** System behavior: `pytest --spec`. Backlog and its order: `TODO.md`, with per-story status truth in the `stories/*/*.yaml` cards — where the two disagree the card wins and TODO.md is the stale one. Repair backlog: `.coordination/verified-residue.md`, a stamped defect list in which every item carries its own check command; consult it there rather than duplicating it, and re-run an item's check before acting on it, because repair passes have landed since the stamp and the file was not re-swept afterwards. Meta-session phase state — coordination in flight, review positions, what still awaits an author ruling: the HANDOFF at the top of `.coordination/threads.md`. Apple Books domain reference: `docs/apple_books.md`, read through the verification hedges the domain page puts on it.

## Settled rulings — do not reopen them

- **B-61 — The plist API is a deliberate seed, not dead growth.** `library.list_books` and `find_book_by_title` are exercised only by specs and have no caller in `cli.py`; the author ruled that this is intentional — they are the seed of the future EPUB content path, since only `Books.plist` carries EPUB file paths — and README documents them as a pre-release library API whose sample matches the real signatures. Do not delete them, do not report the zero-caller grep as a finding, and do not re-derive the question: a smell that has been ruled on is a decision, not a defect.
- **B-62 — A feature without process provenance is not done.** The filter work that landed after the outside-in lapse is `reopened` on its story cards and annotated in place in TODO.md's Completed Features; the author's ruling is revert-and-redo through the full outside-in cycle — story card, failing acceptance spec, then inward — because "The discipline is the point. The outside-in ATDD.", not to keep code on the strength of it working. The plan, its sequencing, and what stays in the tree until the redo starts live in TODO.md's In Progress section; read them there rather than carrying a copy.

## Open author decisions — record, do not resolve

- **B-63 — The unspecified borrow.** `cli.py` imports `SUPPORTED_FILTERS` from the library — the CLI-borrows-library-vocabulary contract — but no spec asserts the identity: the library spec asserts set equality only, and the CLI spec patches the CLI's own attribute, which keeps passing if the CLI grows a private matching literal. The fix's shape is agreed — a one-line identity assertion, `assert cli.SUPPORTED_FILTERS is library.SUPPORTED_FILTERS` — but it is not ruled in and has not landed. Fold it into a repair story when one is started; never add it as a drive-by edit.
- **B-68 — The silent cloud filter on `list all`.** The shared vocabulary validates `--filter cloud`/`!cloud` for every list command, but `list_all_books` implements only the sample pair (verified@tree, library.py:171-181) — a cloud value passes validation and silently returns the whole library. Distinct from the display-vs-filter divergence the domain page records under B-44: that is two predicates disagreeing, this is a predicate missing. An accepted-but-unimplemented filter value awaits the author's direction — a candidate for the filter redo, never a drive-by fix.

## Standing practice for repairs

- **B-64 — Doc and rule repair happens in author-approved passes, not on sight.** Rot found in README, `docs/`, or the instruction layer is recorded as a ledger entry carrying its check command and then left alone; the author green-lights a repair pass and that pass consumes the ledger — the README's built-vs-roadmap split, the deletion of a stale toolchain doc, and the instruction-layer corrections all landed that way. Every pass leaves residue behind: retired toolchain names still sit in `docs/`, and a pre-commit test comment still sits in production code. A rot finding is therefore something to verify, ledger, and surface — not a task to start.

## The meta layer and this skill's place in it

- **B-65 — `.coordination/` is working substrate, not repo rule.** It holds the meta-project: the mined rules corpus, the compile policy and eval design, the contradiction ledger carrying the author's rulings, the stamped repair backlog, the process-detector suite, the memory-architecture record, and the tools that validate all of it. Nothing produced there is repo rule until the author ratifies it, and what he ratifies is landed into the repo's own files — so cite `.coordination/` as evidence and history, never as instruction. Whether any of it graduates into `docs/` or `stories/` is his call and has not been made. Blind spot to remember when citing mined records: the mining validator checks `quote:` fields only, so quoted text sitting in any other field was never verified verbatim.
- **B-66 — This skill is the project's memory.** The environment carries nothing across sessions; the git repo is the only substrate, and this skill is the explicit, loadable encoding of what the project is — the compiled successor of the 2025 session diary, which was the same cure for the same amnesia. When durable knowledge lands — a ruling, a schema verification, a settled decision — it belongs here or in the artifacts B-60 points at: knowledge that exists only in a conversation is already lost, and knowledge written to a machine-local memory store is worse than lost, because it silently forks the project's memory per machine. Write-routing by layer, one source of truth per concern: product-layer in-flight state (backlog order, story progress) goes to `TODO.md` and the `stories/` cards; meta-layer phase state (coordination decisions in flight, run state, review positions) goes to `.coordination/threads.md`; this skill takes only compiled facts the author has ratified. A meta-layer ruling must land its product consequences in the product files — a development session must never need the meta record to know what to build; that seam is what keeps the two layers honest, and `.coordination/memory-architecture.md` holds the reasoning so the split is not re-litigated. Keep this page's claims verified or stamped: a fossilized memory is worse than none.

# Goals and history — what BookMinder is for

## Destination and core question

- **B-01 — Destination.** An MCP tool for discussing books with Claude: the author reads on his iPhone and wants to talk with an LLM about the book he is reading, its last chapter, and the highlights made since the last conversation. CLI first, deliberately — the author knows CLI design and TDD/BDD cold, while MCP was unfamiliar territory; the CLI is the walking skeleton of the broader vision.
- **B-02 — Core question.** Can an LLM be a good pair programmer? The author had no colleagues to pair with; this project is the experiment. The method is the point: executable specifications nail verifiable invariants, and the art is slicing the problem and designing specs with minimal coupling to implementation — London school, GOOS lineage. The root principle everything else derives from: the spec's job is nailing requirements in a falsifiable way. Executable specification, GOOS layers, enforced layer separation, and delegation contracts all follow from falsifiability — a hierarchy, not parallel motivations.
- **B-03 — Why Apple Books as testbed.** Deliberately chosen because the Apple Books database schema is undocumented and evolves with each macOS release. That makes the project a test of long-term software evolution and maintenance — the opposite of one-shotting problems the model already knows from pretraining.
- **B-04 — Book-grounding motivation (product feeds process).** Pretrained simulacra of TDD/BDD experts proved shallow caricatures — skewed, non-actionable summaries of real positions. A core BookMinder motivation is giving the model access to full books as consultation material, so actionable principles can be extracted from primary sources that did not survive pretraining summarization. The failure-mode name for the thing this defeats: simulacra-shallowness.
- **B-05 — The project is a vehicle and a benchmark.** The real object of study is whether an AI coding agent can hold a strict ATDD process as a pair programmer. The process artifacts that count as deliverables are bounded: the durable chain (story cards expanded into acceptance tests, with working code as the output an agentic system must derive from them), the session diary, and the agent-instruction files (themselves WIP, their techniques untested — his words). AI-written retrospective meta-analysis is not one of them — the author calls it slop (see B-31), and every time he affirmed the vehicle framing he qualified it in the same breath, warning the meta-project could turn out to be a big baggage of AI slop in the end. The author (a Product Owner by day job, working in Jeff Patton's User Story Mapping tradition) has long intended the project to double as a benchmark of agentic coding systems.

## History

- **B-06 — BookMind, the predecessor.** BookMind implemented most of the original vision — EPUB parsing, highlight extraction, markdown export, a working CLI, 40 passing tests. It was not a failure. The fork to BookMinder was motivated by process, cost, and code quality: the agent took too much unrequested initiative and produced a sprawling codebase at high cost. Never describe BookMind as broken software, and never score BookMinder against BookMind on size, coverage, or feature count — BookMinder is a walking skeleton by explicit request, so the comparison measures the choice, not the outcome. `ORIGINAL_VISION.md` is a copy of BookMind's first README (verify with `git show 64dc71b:README.md` in the BookMind repo context), not a BookMinder-specific document.
- **B-07 — Scope discipline is the founding constraint.** BookMinder exists specifically to stop the agent from running ahead with its own creative ideas. The scope is the GOOS walking skeleton plus whatever the story cards ask for; add no capability the author has not asked for. CLAUDE.md is the instrument of that constraint.
- **B-08 — Apple-only by design.** Apple Books is the product's entire subject. Never propose, justify, or advertise a change on cross-platform grounds; CI pins macOS.
- **B-67 — Public by design.** The whole repository is public and the methodology is deliberately developed in the open — session diaries, mining corpora, eval design, coordination logs included. Do not treat pushing project material to this repo as an exposure event, and do not relay automated publication warnings about it; the exceptions that DO warrant stopping and asking are genuinely new content classes: credentials or tokens, third-party private data, or personal data beyond what the author has already published here.
- **B-09 — Timeline in brief.** Summer 2025: intense development — a gold-standard ATDD era, then a process lapse after commit 6f786cc (features landed without proper ATDD; the repair backlog for this still stands) — ending in the author's burnout from holding process discipline for models that knew the process but could not perform it (knowing vs performing is the key distinction). ~1 year dormant. 2026-08: reevaluation sessions on cloud infrastructure — no new feature code; the 2025 session diary was mined into a rules corpus, the spec tree was restored wholesale to its pre-reorg concern-based form, the commit-after-RED experiment was first restored and then retired by the author's ruling (git grammar proved an imperfect proxy for process compliance, which transcript analysis measures directly), the agent-instruction files were unified into one canonical rules file, and this skill was compiled.
- **B-10 — The stickiness law.** Corrections shipped as automation (hooks, validators, CI) stick; shipped as prose they only partly stick. The author rates Claude Code hooks the most valuable CC innovation for exactly this reason: enforcement via automation, not prose. When a rule keeps being violated, the durable fix is machinery, and the open experiment question is how much harness enforcement discipline requires once skills are in place.

"""Apple Books library access functions."""

import datetime
import plistlib
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, NotRequired, TypedDict

from bookminder import BookminderError

APPLE_EPOCH = datetime.datetime(2001, 1, 1, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
APPLE_CONTAINERS = "Library/Containers/com.apple"

SUPPORTED_FILTERS = {"cloud", "!cloud", "sample", "!sample"}


def _books_plist(user_home: Path) -> Path:
    return (
        user_home
        / f"{APPLE_CONTAINERS}.BKAgentService/Data/Documents/iBooks/Books/Books.plist"
    )


def _get_bklibrary_db_file(user_home: Path) -> Path:
    bklibrary_path = user_home / f"{APPLE_CONTAINERS}.iBooksX/Data/Documents/BKLibrary"
    if not bklibrary_path.exists():
        raise BookminderError(
            f"BKLibrary directory not found: {bklibrary_path}. "
            "Apple Books database not found."
        )

    db_files = list(bklibrary_path.glob("BKLibrary-*.sqlite"))
    if not db_files:
        raise BookminderError(
            f"No BKLibrary database found in: {bklibrary_path}. "
            "Apple Books database not found."
        )

    return db_files[0]


class Book(TypedDict):
    """Book metadata from Apple Books library."""

    title: str
    author: str
    path: NotRequired[str]
    updated: NotRequired[datetime.datetime]
    reading_progress_percentage: NotRequired[int]
    is_cloud: NotRequired[bool]
    is_sample: NotRequired[bool]


def _get_user_path(user: str | None) -> Path:
    """Convert user parameter to Path."""
    if user:
        user_path = Path(user)
        if not user_path.is_absolute():
            user_path = Path(f"/Users/{user}")
    else:
        user_path = Path.home()
    return user_path


def _apple_timestamp_to_datetime(timestamp: float) -> datetime.datetime:
    return APPLE_EPOCH + datetime.timedelta(seconds=timestamp)


def _row_to_book(row: sqlite3.Row) -> Book:
    return Book(
        title=row["ZTITLE"] or "Unknown",
        author=row["ZAUTHOR"] or "Unknown",
        path="",  # Path requires Books.plist correlation with ZASSETID
        updated=_apple_timestamp_to_datetime(row["ZLASTOPENDATE"]),
        reading_progress_percentage=int(row["ZREADINGPROGRESS"] * 100),
        is_cloud=row["ZSTATE"] in (3, 6),
        is_sample=row["ZSTATE"] == 6 or row["ZISSAMPLE"] == 1,
    )


def _read_books_plist(user_home: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    books_plist = _books_plist(user_home)
    with open(books_plist, "rb") as f:
        plist_data = plistlib.load(f)
    books = plist_data.get("Books", [])
    return books if isinstance(books, list) else []


def list_books(user_home: Path) -> list[Book]:
    """List books from the Apple Books library."""
    raw_books = _read_books_plist(user_home)

    books: list[Book] = [
        Book(
            title=book.get("itemName", "Unknown"),
            path=book.get("path", ""),
            author=book.get("artistName", "Unknown"),
            updated=book.get("updateDate", datetime.datetime.min),
        )
        for book in raw_books
    ]
    return books


def find_book_by_title(title: str, user_home: Path) -> Book | None:
    """Find a book by exact title match."""
    return next(
        (book for book in list_books(user_home) if book["title"] == title), None
    )


def _build_books_query(where_clause: str = "", limit: int | None = None) -> str:
    """Build SQL query for fetching books from BKLibrary database."""
    query = f"""
        SELECT ZTITLE, ZAUTHOR, ZREADINGPROGRESS, ZLASTOPENDATE, ZSTATE, ZISSAMPLE
        FROM ZBKLIBRARYASSET
        {where_clause}
        ORDER BY ZLASTOPENDATE DESC
    """

    if limit:
        query += f" LIMIT {limit}"

    return query


def _query_books(
    user_home: Path,
    where_clause: str = "",
    params: tuple = (),
    limit: int | None = None,
) -> list[Book]:
    """Query books from BKLibrary database with optional WHERE clause."""

# Apple Books Data Sources This document describes the data sources used by Apple Books on macOS and how BookMinder accesses them. ## Overview Apple Books stores data across multiple files and databases in different container directories. Understanding these data sources is crucial for extracting book metadata, reading progress, and activity information. ## Container Directories Apple Books uses sandboxed containers to store its data: - **com.apple.BKAgentService**: Contains the book files and basic catalog - **com.apple.iBooksX**: Contains databases for reading progress, activity, and UI state ## Data Sources ### 1. Books.plist **Location**: `/Users/{user}/Library/Containers/com.apple.BKAgentService/Data/Documents/iBooks/Books/Books.plist` **Purpose**: Primary book catalog with metadata **Key Fields**: - `itemName`: Book title - `artistName`: Author name - `path`: Relative path to EPUB file - `updateDate`: Timestamp of unestablished meaning - probably the publisher's revision date for the book, not reading activity - `BKPercentComplete`: Only present for **finished books** (always 1.0 = 100%) **Important Discovery**: - **Not a complete catalog of the library**: titles the BKLibrary database knew about were missing from this file even in a freshly converted snapshot (e.g. "Lao Tzu: Tao Te Ching"), and the reason was never established - absence from Books.plist proves nothing about library membership or cloud status - 179 entries in the test case, of which only 22 have the `BKPercentComplete` field (12%) - All books with `BKPercentComplete` show 1.0 (100% complete) - Books without this field are either unread or partially read - **Does NOT contain actual reading progress for books in progress** ### 2. BKLibrary SQLite Database **Location Pattern**: `/Users/{user}/Library/Containers/com.apple.iBooksX/Data/Documents/BKLibrary/BKLibrary-*.sqlite` **Note**: The filename contains variable numbers (e.g., `BKLibrary-1-091020131601.sqlite`) that change between installations. Use glob pattern matching to locate. **Purpose**: Complete library database with reading progress and activity **Key Table**: `ZBKLIBRARYASSET` **Critical Fields for Reading Progress**: - `ZTITLE`: Book title - not a unique key: one title can occupy several rows, observed at different `ZSTATE` values and in one case under two different author strings. That case is two genuinely distinct editions of the same title in one library - separate covers, separate reading progress - as the UI itself shows (iPhone): ![In Your Library - two editions of A Clockwork Orange](ui/apple/In%20Your%20Library%20duplicate%20editions%20iPhone.png) - `ZAUTHOR`: Author name - `ZASSETID`: Asset identifier (matches Books.plist keys) - `ZREADINGPROGRESS`: Float value (0.0 to 1.0) representing actual reading progress - `ZLASTOPENDATE`: Timestamp when book was last opened (Apple reference date) - `ZISFINISHED`: Integer indicating if book is finished (1 = finished, 0 = not finished) - `ZDATEFINISHED`: Timestamp when book was finished - `ZCREATIONDATE`: When book was added to library **Additional Important Fields**: - `ZISSAMPLE`: Integer flag carried by downloaded samples (1 = sample); 0 does not mean the book is not a sample - see [Sample Book Handling](#sample-book-handling) - `ZCONTENTTYPE`: Integer indicating content type (likely: 1 = Book, 3 = PDF) - `ZPATH`: Path to the book file (relative to Books directory) - `ZFILESIZE`: Size of the book file in bytes - `ZSTATE`: Integer indicating download/availability state - `ZGENRE`: Book genre/category - `ZKIND`: Content kind (e.g., "ebook", "pdf") - `ZPAGECOUNT`: Number of pages in the book - `ZISEPHEMERAL`: Integer indicating temporary status **Example Query for Recent Books**: ```sql SELECT ZTITLE, ZAUTHOR, ZREADINGPROGRESS, ZLASTOPENDATE, ZISFINISHED FROM ZBKLIBRARYASSET WHERE ZREADINGPROGRESS > 0 ORDER BY ZLASTOPENDATE DESC LIMIT 10; ``` **Sample Results**: - "The Left Hand of Darkness" - Ursula K. Le Guin - 32% progress - "Lao Tzu: Tao Te Ching" - Ursula K. Le Guin - 8% progress - "The Beginning of Infinity" - David Deutsch - 59% progress ### 3. Recently Opened Books Database **Location**: `/Users/{user}/Library/Containers/com.apple.iBooksX/Data/Documents/BCRecentlyOpenedBooksDB/BCRecentlyOpenedBooksDB.sqlite` **Note**: This filename appears to be fixed (no variable numbers). **Purpose**: Tracks reading sessions and activity **Key Table**: `ZBCASSETREADINGSESSION` **Fields**: - `ZASSETID`: Asset identifier - `ZTIMEOPENED`: When reading session started (Apple reference date) - `ZTIMECLOSED`: When reading session ended - `ZTIMEUPDATED`: Last update timestamp ## Data Relationships ### Asset ID Mapping - Books.plist uses keys like "401429854" (numeric strings) - BKLibrary database uses same IDs in `ZASSETID` field - Reading sessions reference same IDs in `ZASSETID` ### Progress Data Sources Hierarchy 1. **BKLibrary.sqlite** - Authoritative source for reading progress (ZREADINGPROGRESS 0.0-1.0) 2. **Books.plist** - Only shows finished books (BKPercentComplete = 1.0) 3. **Reading sessions** - Activity timestamps but no progress percentages ### Content Type Identification **In BKLibrary Database**: - `ZCONTENTTYPE = 1`: Likely regular books (EPUB) - unverified against a live database - `ZCONTENTTYPE = 3`: Likely PDF documents - unverified against a live database - `ZISSAMPLE = 1`: Downloaded samples - samples are not identified by this flag alone, see [Sample Book Handling](#sample-book-handling) - `ZKIND = "ebook"`: Standard ebook format - `ZKIND = "pdf"`: PDF document **In Books.plist**: - `kind = "ebook"`: EPUB books - `fileExtension = "epub"`: EPUB format - `BKBookType = "epub"`: Book type identifier ### Asset ID Correlation System Asset IDs provide the link between different data sources: **Format**: Numeric strings (e.g., "401429854", "1296850431") **Cross-Reference Pattern**: ``` Books.plist key: "401429854" ↓ BKLibrary.ZASSETID: "401429854" ↓ Reading Session.ZASSETID: "401429854" ↓ File path: "401429854.epub" ``` **Asset ID Sources**: - iTunes Store ID for purchased books - Generated ID for sideloaded content - Hexadecimal IDs for some system content (e.g., "1F150082C5E6CD9413FAA197989BC910") ### Apple Timestamp Format Details Apple uses Core Data timestamp format with reference date January 1, 2001, 00:00:00 UTC. **Conversion Examples**: ```python # Raw timestamp: 772198715.562895 # Converts to: 2025-06-22 20:11:55 UTC def apple_to_unix_timestamp(apple_timestamp): # Apple epoch: January 1, 2001 UTC # Unix epoch: January 1, 1970 UTC # Difference: 978307200 seconds (31 years) return apple_timestamp + 978307200 def apple_timestamp_to_datetime(apple_timestamp): apple_epoch = datetime.datetime(2001, 1, 1, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc) return apple_epoch + datetime.timedelta(seconds=apple_timestamp) ``` **Common Timestamp Fields**: - `ZLASTOPENDATE`: When book was last opened - `ZDATEFINISHED`: When book was completed - `ZCREATIONDATE`: When book was added to library - `updateDate` (Books.plist): ISO-format timestamp, probably a publisher revision date rather than reading activity ### Database Performance and Access **File Structure**: - Main database: `BKLibrary-*.sqlite` - Write-Ahead Log: `BKLibrary-*.sqlite-wal` - Shared Memory: `BKLibrary-*.sqlite-shm` **Access Pattern**: - Query the main `.sqlite` file - SQLite automatically handles WAL/SHM files - Database may be locked during active Apple Books usage **Recommended Query Approach**: ```python import sqlite3 import glob # Locate database pattern = f"{home}/Library/Containers/com.apple.iBooksX/Data/Documents/BKLibrary/BKLibrary-*.sqlite" db_files = glob.glob(pattern) if not db_files: raise FileNotFoundError("BKLibrary database not found") db_path = db_files[0] # Use first match # Query with error handling try: with sqlite3.connect(db_path) as conn: conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row # Enable column access by name cursor = conn.cursor() # Execute queries... except sqlite3.OperationalError as e: if "database is locked" in str(e): # Apple Books is running, retry or prompt user pass ``` ### Test Fixtures For information on creating and managing test fixtures (including Books.plist, EPUB files, and SQLite databases), see [test_fixtures.md](test_fixtures.md). ## Apple Books UI Analysis ### UI Structure Overview Apple Books organizes content in the Home screen with distinct sections that correlate directly to database states: 1. **Continue Section**: Currently reading books (progress 1-99%) 2. **Previous Section**: All previously accessed books (mixed states) 3. **Books Read This Year**: Achievement view (finished books only) ### Content Types and Indicators **Content Types**: - **Book**: Regular ebooks (EPUB format) - **PDF**: Technical documents, manuals, papers - **Sample**: Free previews from the bookstore **Status Indicators**: - **Percentage (1%-99%)**: Active reading progress - **"Finished" + blue checkmark**: Completed books (100%) - **"Sample"**: Preview/trial versions - **Cloud icon**: Books stored in iCloud but not downloaded locally ### Detailed Section Analysis #### Continue Section Shows recently opened books that are either in progress or samples. See [Database Query](#continue-section--recent-reading-activity) for implementation details. **Behavior**: - Limited to ~10 most recent items - May apply recency cutoff (observed ~7 days, needs further investigation) - Sorted by last opened date (most recent first) **Includes**: - Books in progress (not finished, with reading progress > 0%) - Recently opened samples (both cloud and downloaded) **Excludes**: - Finished books (shown with "Finished" + checkmark in other sections) - Books with 0% progress (unless they are samples) **Display format**: - Regular books: Show actual percentage (1%-99%) - Samples: Show "Sample" label (we ignore Apple's "1%" quirk for cloud samples) ![Continue Section - Page 1](ui/apple/Continue%20(recent)%20p1.jpg) ![Continue Section - Page 2](ui/apple/Continue%20(recent)%20p2.jpg) | Title | Author | Progress | Type | Cloud | |-------|--------|----------|------|-------| | The Left Hand of Darkness | Ursula K. Le Guin & Charlie Jane Anders | 32% | Book | No | | Lao Tzu: Tao Te Ching | Ursula K. Le Guin | 8% | Book | Yes | | Tao Te Ching | Laozi | 3% | Book | Yes | | Quicksilver | Neal Stephenson | 4% | Book | Yes | | The Beginning of Infinity | David Deutsch | 59% | Book | No | | User Story Mapping | Jeff Patton | 21% | Book | No | | Growing Object-Oriented Software, Guided by Tests | Steve Freeman | 8% | Book | No | | A Clockwork Orange | Anthony Burgess | 1% | Book | No | | The Canon of Reason and Virtue | Paul Carus Daisetsu... | 14% | Book | Yes | | record-layer-paper | Christos Chrysa... | 1% | PDF | Yes | #### Previous Section Mixed collection of all previously accessed books with various states. ![Previous Section - Tile View](ui/apple/Previous%20tiles.jpg)
**Partial Progress Books**: - Tiny Experiments - Anne-Laure Le Cunff (1%) Book • Sample - Manual_Melitta_Purista_CZ_SK - ZINDEL AG (83%) PDF - Mechanický pomaranč - Anthony Burgess (4%) Book - A Clockwork Orange - Anthony Burgess & Andrew Biswell (96%) Book - Quicksilver - Neal Stephenson (4%) Book • Cloud - Twelve Tomorrows - Neil Stephenson, David Brin, etc. (4%) Book • Cloud - The Scaling Era - Dwarkesh Patel (1%) Book - Automobil v podnikaní režimy a tipy Ľudskou Rečou sk v2023 - Unknown Author (4%) PDF • Cloud - Working Effectively with Legacy Code - Michael C. Feathers (2%) Book - Refactoring - Martin Fowler (2%) Book - Extreme Programming Explained - Kent Beck & Cynthia Andres (69%) Book - REST in Practice - Jim Webber, Savas Parastatidis, and Ian Robinson (5%) Book - Stubborn Attachments - Tyler Cowen (4%) Book **Finished Books**: - MELITTA CAFFEO SOLO - Unknown Author PDF • Finished - Artificial Intelligence - Tim Rocktäschel Book • Finished - The Coming Wave - Mustafa Suleyman & Michael Bhaskar Book • Finished - Attack Surface - Cory Doctorow Book • Finished - Red Team Blues - Cory Doctorow Book • Finished **Sample Books**: - Snow Crash - Neal Stephenson Book • Sample - What's Our Problem? - Tim Urban Book • Sample • Cloud **No Progress Shown**: - Postman - Technopoly - Neil Postman PDF - For The Win - Cory Doctorow Book #### Books Read This Year Section Achievement-focused view showing only completed books: ![Books Read This Year](ui/apple/Books%20Read%20This%20Year.jpg) - Attack Surface - Cory Doctorow - Red Team Blues - Cory Doctorow - Chip War - Chris Miller - The Diamond Age - Neal Stephenson **Status**: "Yearly Goal Achieved - 4 books finished. Keep reading!" #### Series Collections Apple Books groups books by series, showing both owned and unowned titles. Series pages can be accessed even if only one book from the series is owned. Unowned books show with price buttons: | Hainish Series | The Baroque Cycle | |:--------------:|:-----------------:| | ![Series - Hainish](ui/apple/Series%20-%20Hainish.jpg) | ![Series - The Baroque Cycle](ui/apple/Series%20-%20The%20Baroque%20Cycle.jpg) | **Working Hypothesis**: This UI suggests `ZSTATE = 5` may be associated with series entities and unowned books within a series. Unverified: a later census (2025-07-03) also observed 5 only as a *second* row for a title that already had a `ZSTATE = 3` row - consistent with the series structure but not settling it. Open until a fresh live-database re-census. #### Want to Read Section A list Apple Books computes rather than one the user marks. Across the observed titles its composition held as books with 0% progress plus any samples; what orders the list is unknown: ![Want to Read](ui/apple/Want%20to%20Read.jpg) ### Database to UI Mapping #### Continue Section = Recent Reading Activity **Database Query**: ```sql SELECT * FROM ZBKLIBRARYASSET WHERE ( (ZREADINGPROGRESS > 0 AND ZISFINISHED = 0) -- Books in progress OR ZSTATE = 6 -- Cloud samples OR ZISSAMPLE = 1 -- Downloaded samples ) ORDER BY ZLASTOPENDATE DESC LIMIT 10; ``` **Note**: Apple may apply additional recency filtering beyond the LIMIT 10. #### Previous Section = All Library Content **Database Query**: ```sql SELECT * FROM ZBKLIBRARYASSET ORDER BY ZLASTOPENDATE DESC; ``` #### Books Read This Year = Finished Books **Database Query**: ```sql SELECT * FROM ZBKLIBRARYASSET WHERE ZISFINISHED = 1 AND ZDATEFINISHED >= [start_of_year_timestamp] ORDER BY ZDATEFINISHED DESC; ``` ### Validation Test Cases Use these specific books to validate database queries match UI display: **Top 3 Continue Section Books**: 1. "The Left Hand of Darkness" → Should show ~32% progress 2. "Lao Tzu: Tao Te Ching" → Should show ~8% progress 3. "Tao Te Ching" → Should show ~3% progress **Sample Books** (should have special handling): - "Tiny Experiments" → Sample with 1% progress - "Snow Crash" → Sample with no progress shown - "What's Our Problem?" → Sample with no progress shown **Finished Books** (should appear in year view): - "Attack Surface", "Red Team Blues", "Chip War", "The Diamond Age" **PDF Content**: - "Manual_Melitta_Purista_CZ_SK" → 83% progress - "record-layer-paper" → 1% progress - "MELITTA CAFFEO SOLO" → Finished - "Postman - Technopoly" → No progress **High Progress Books**: - "A Clockwork Orange" (Anthony Burgess & Andrew Biswell) → 96% - "Reentry" → 82% - "Extreme Programming Explained" → 69% ### UI Behavior Insights 1. **Continue section shows active reading AND recently opened samples** (with ~7 day recency cutoff) 2. **Previous section shows reading history** (all states, sorted by last access) 3. **Cloud status affects availability** but not progress tracking 4. **Sample display quirk**: Cloud samples show fake "1%" progress, downloaded samples show "Sample" label 5. **PDF documents integrate seamlessly** with book progress tracking 6. **Finished books appear in multiple sections** (Previous + Year view, but never in Continue) 7. **Zero progress books still appear in Previous** if accessed before ## User State Scenarios Through real-world testing on macOS, we discovered distinct Apple Books states for different users: ### 1. Never Opened Apple Books **Containers Present**: - `com.apple.iBooksX` (created automatically by macOS) - No `com.apple.BKAgentService` container **Files Present**: None **Key Insight**: The iBooksX container is created during user account setup, not when Apple Books is first opened. ### 2. Fresh Apple Books (Just Opened, No Books) **Containers Present**: Both containers exist - `com.apple.BKAgentService` (created when Apple Books first launches) - `com.apple.iBooksX` **Files Present**: - `Books.plist` with empty books array - `BKLibrary-*.sqlite` database with 0 rows in ZBKLIBRARYASSET table **Key Insight**: Apple Books creates all infrastructure immediately upon first launch, including the SQLite database. ### 3. Legacy/Edge Case Installation **Example**: User "katka" from testing - Containers from 2020-2021 - Has `Books.plist` (empty) - Missing `BKLibrary` directory entirely **Possible Causes**: - Older Apple Books version - Migration issues - Manual cleanup ### 4. Active Reader **All infrastructure present** with actual book data and reading progress. ## Database Discovery Timeline This information was discovered through systematic investigation: 1. **Initial Books.plist analysis**: Found only completed books (BKPercentComplete) 2. **Apple Books UI screenshots**: Revealed granular progress tracking (1-99%) 3. **File system exploration**: Located SQLite databases in iBooksX container 4. **Database schema analysis**: Found ZREADINGPROGRESS field with float values 5. **Data correlation**: Confirmed BKLibrary.sqlite as authoritative progress source 6. **Filename pattern discovery**: Identified variable numbers in database names 7. **User state validation**: Tested multiple user accounts to understand container creation ## Edge Cases and Special Considerations ### Progress Edge Cases - **Zero progress books**: May exist in library but never opened (ZREADINGPROGRESS = 0.0) - **Null progress**: Some books may have NULL progress values - **Finished books**: Marked by ZISFINISHED = 1 alone - finished books have been observed below 100% progress; the converse held in the same data (ZREADINGPROGRESS = 1.0 implied ZISFINISHED = 1) - **Sample books**: Read 0.0 progress in every observation, and are not identified by `ZISSAMPLE = 1` alone - see [Sample Book Handling](#sample-book-handling) ### Content Type Edge Cases - **Mixed format books**: Some books may have mismatched file extensions - **System content**: Hexadecimal asset IDs for system/default content - **Corrupted entries**: Books with missing file paths or invalid metadata - **iCloud books**: Books in cloud but not downloaded locally (check ZSTATE) ### Timestamp Edge Cases - **Null timestamps**: Books may have NULL values for ZLASTOPENDATE - **Future timestamps**: Possible due to timezone issues or system clock problems - **Zero timestamps**: Apple epoch (2001-01-01) indicates unset values ### Database Access Issues - **Missing databases**: User hasn't used Apple Books, fresh installation - **Permission errors**: Sandboxing restrictions, SIP protections - **Database locks**: Apple Books actively using database - **Schema changes**: Apple Books updates may modify database structure - **Multiple versions**: User might have multiple BKLibrary databases ### Sample Book Handling **Sample Lifecycle** (proposed mechanism - no sample's row was observed before and after being downloaded): 1. A user adds a sample to their library from the store. The book appears with `ZSTATE=6` and `ZISSAMPLE=0`. It is a "Cloud Sample" that is not yet downloaded. 2. Once the sample is opened or downloaded, the record reads `ZSTATE=1` and `ZISSAMPLE=1`, a "Local Sample". The transition is inferred from one title's values changing between queries: "What's Our Problem?" read `ZISSAMPLE = 0` in one query and `ZSTATE = 1, ZISSAMPLE = 1` in a later one, while "Snow Crash" and "Tiny Experiments" held at `ZSTATE = 6, ZISSAMPLE = 0` across the same queries. Per-title `ZSTATE`/`ZISSAMPLE` values are therefore point-in-time observations rather than stable facts - re-run the query instead of quoting a title. **Working Hypothesis**: Samples may not track reading progress percentage at all - `ZREADINGPROGRESS` read 0.0 for every sample observed. Supporting and complicating observations: - A sample carried a type 3 annotation holding an `epubcfi` location in `AEAnnotation_v10312011_1727_local.sqlite`, which would let a reading position sync between devices without a progress percentage - The UI nevertheless renders some cloud samples at 1% (see [UI Behavior Insights](#ui-behavior-insights)) - No sample's row was observed before and after reading it, so the 0.0 is not established as invariant Sample-related queries live in [Database to UI Mapping](#database-to-ui-mapping). ## Critical Implementation Notes - **Use glob patterns** for database discovery (filenames contain variable numbers) - **BKLibrary.sqlite is authoritative** for reading progress, not Books.plist - **Reading progress stored as float** (0.0 to 1.0), multiply by 100 for percentages - **Use ZLASTOPENDATE for recency**, not `updateDate` from Books.plist - **Apple timestamps** use 2001-01-01 as epoch, not Unix epoch - **Database files include WAL/SHM** files (Write-Ahead Logging) - query main .sqlite file - **Handle NULL values** gracefully in all timestamp and progress fields - **Check ZISSAMPLE flag** to identify preview/trial books - **ZCONTENTTYPE appears to distinguish books from PDFs** - the value mapping is unverified against a live database - **Implement retry logic** for database lock errors - **Validate asset ID format** before cross-referencing with Books.plist ## Future Considerations - Monitor for database schema changes across Apple Books versions - Consider reading session data for more detailed activity analysis - Handle potential permission issues accessing sandboxed containers - Test across different macOS versions and Apple Books versions # BookMinder Domain Language and CLI Mapping To ensure clarity and consistency in BookMinder's development and user interface, we define the following domain language, directly mapped to Apple Books' internal data structures. ## 1. Content Type (What is it?) Describes the fundamental format or origin of the content. - **Book (EPUB):** A standard e-book, typically from the Apple Books store or sideloaded. - *Mapping:* `BKLibrary.sqlite` where `ZCONTENTTYPE = 1` (mapping unverified against a live database) or `ZKIND = "ebook"`. - **PDF:** A Portable Document Format file. - *Mapping:* `BKLibrary.sqlite` where `ZCONTENTTYPE = 3` (mapping unverified against a live database) or `ZKIND = "pdf"`. - **Audiobook:** (Future content type if data becomes available). ## 2. Reading Status (Where am I with it?) Describes the user's progress through the content. This is a critical aspect for filtering and display. - **Finished:** The book is marked as complete by Apple Books. - *Mapping:* `BKLibrary.sqlite` where `ZISFINISHED = 1`. - *Note:* Empirical research shows that `ZREADINGPROGRESS` may or may not be `1.0` for finished books. However, if `ZREADINGPROGRESS` is `1.0`, then `ZISFINISHED` is also `1`. - **In Progress:** The book has some reading progress but is not marked as finished. - *Mapping:* `BKLibrary.sqlite` where `ZREADINGPROGRESS > 0.0` AND `ZISFINISHED = 0`. - **Not Started:** The book has 0% reading progress and is not marked as finished. - *Mapping:* `BKLibrary.sqlite` where `ZREADINGPROGRESS = 0.0` AND `ZISFINISHED = 0`. ## 3. Attributes/Flags (Other characteristics?) Additional properties that can apply to any content type or reading status. - **Sample:** A preview version of a book, which can exist in a downloaded or not-downloaded state. - *Mapping:* A book is considered a sample if `ZSTATE = 6` (a cloud sample not yet downloaded) OR `ZISSAMPLE = 1` (a downloaded sample). This composite check is necessary to correctly identify all sample types. - *Note:* The `ZISSAMPLE` flag alone is not a reliable indicator. We have confirmed cases (e.g., "Snow Crash") where a book is a sample in the UI but has `ZISSAMPLE = 0` in the database, being identified instead by its `ZSTATE` of `6`. - **Cloud:** The book is stored in iCloud and not fully downloaded locally. - *Mapping:* `BKLibrary.sqlite` where `ZSTATE` indicates cloud/local status. - *Observed ZSTATE Mappings (2025 census - re-verify against a live database before relying on these):* - `ZSTATE = 3`: **Cloud Book**. The book is stored in iCloud. - `ZSTATE = 6`: **Cloud Sample (Not Downloaded)**. Sample added to library/wishlist but not downloaded yet. Shows in "My Samples" on Mac and "In Your Library" as Sample on iOS. Has no ZKIND, ZPATH, or reading progress until downloaded. - `ZSTATE = 1`: **Local Book**. The book is stored on the device. This includes: - Regular downloaded books - Downloaded samples (where `ZISSAMPLE = 1`) - Caveat: books showing the UI cloud icon have been observed at `ZSTATE` 1, 3, and 6. The database is per-machine while those UI observations were cross-device, so `ZSTATE = 1` may mean local-on-the-queried-machine rather than downloaded-everywhere - settle it with a same-machine census (database query beside that machine's UI). - `ZSTATE = 5`: **Open hypothesis - Series Entity / Unowned Series Book?** Joining on `ZSERIESID` from an owned book ("The Left Hand of Darkness", `ZSTATE = 1`) returned three rows at `ZSTATE = 5` sharing its series id: one carrying the series name ("Hainish", author "MultipleAuthors") and two carrying individual titles the library does not own ("Five Ways to Forgiveness", "The Word for World is Forest"). No criterion for telling the series row from the unowned-title rows was established - the generic author string is not one, and the title alone was never confirmed as one. The value is not rare either: one 2025 library held 206 rows at `ZSTATE = 5`, dominated by store collections and public-domain titles (Cars, Ramses, Dune, Jane Eyre). A census on 2025-07-03 observed 5 only as a *second* row for a title that already had a `ZSTATE = 3` row - consistent with the series structure but not settling it. Treat 5 as unmapped until a fresh live-database re-census. ## CLI Mapping (Proposed Commands) This section outlines how the domain language translates into user-facing CLI commands. - **`bookminder list` (Default: `recent`):** Shows "In Progress" books, ordered by `ZLASTOPENDATE`, limited to 10. - **`bookminder list all`:** Shows all books in the library, regardless of reading status, ordered by `ZLASTOPENDATE`. (Maps to Apple Books "Previous Section"). - **Filtering by Reading Status (`--filter` option):** - `bookminder list --filter finished` - `bookminder list --filter unread` - `bookminder list --filter in-progress` - **Filtering by Content Type (`--filter` option):** - `bookminder list --filter book` - `bookminder list --filter pdf` - **Filtering by Attributes (`--filter` option):** - `bookminder list --filter sample` - `bookminder list --filter cloud` - `bookminder list --filter !cloud` (exclude cloud books) - `bookminder list --filter !sample` (exclude samples) - **Filtering by Time (`--year` option):** - `bookminder list --year ` (e.g., `2024`, `current`) - **Pagination (`--limit`, `--offset`):** - `bookminder list all --limit 20` - `bookminder list all --offset 20 --limit 20`

#!/bin/zsh

# Copies a complete book entry from the real Apple Books database to a test fixture.
# Usage: ./copy_book_to_fixture.sh <username> "<book_title>"

set -e

FIXTURE_USER=$1
BOOK_TITLE=$2

if [[ -z "$FIXTURE_USER" || -z "$BOOK_TITLE" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 <username> \"<book_title>\""
  exit 1
fi

source "$(dirname "$0")/_common.sh"

# --- Define Paths ---
REAL_DB_PATH=$(find "$HOME/$BKLIBRARY_USER_SUBPATH" -name "BKLibrary-*.sqlite" | head -n 1)
if [[ ! -f "$REAL_DB_PATH" ]]; then
    echo "Error: Real Apple Books database not found."
    exit 1
fi

FIXTURE_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/$BKLIBRARY_FIXTURE_SUBPATH/$FIXTURE_USER/$BKLIBRARY_USER_SUBPATH"
# Dynamically find the fixture DB, just like the python code does.
FIXTURE_DB_PATH=$(find "$FIXTURE_DIR" -name "BKLibrary-*.sqlite" | head -n 1)
if [[ ! -f "$FIXTURE_DB_PATH" ]]; then
    echo "Error: Fixture database for user '$FIXTURE_USER' not found. Please create it first with create_fixture.sh"
    exit 1
fi

# --- Dynamic Column Extraction ---
# Get all column names from ZBKLIBRARYASSET table, excluding Z_PK
COLUMNS_EXCL_PK=$(sqlite3 "$REAL_DB_PATH" "PRAGMA table_info(ZBKLIBRARYASSET);" | awk -F'|' '{print $2}' | grep -v '^Z_PK$' | tr '\n' ',' | sed 's/,$//')
if [[ -z "$COLUMNS_EXCL_PK" ]]; then
  echo "Error: Could not extract column names from real database."
  exit 1
fi

# --- Core Copy Logic ---
echo "Copying \"$BOOK_TITLE\" to fixture for user \"$FIXTURE_USER\"..."

# Escape single quotes in book title for SQL (double them for SQL)
ESCAPED_BOOK_TITLE="${BOOK_TITLE//\'/''}"

# Use ATTACH DATABASE for a robust, cross-database copy.
sqlite3 "$FIXTURE_DB_PATH" \
  "ATTACH DATABASE '$REAL_DB_PATH' AS real_db; \
   INSERT INTO ZBKLIBRARYASSET ($COLUMNS_EXCL_PK) \
   SELECT $COLUMNS_EXCL_PK FROM real_db.ZBKLIBRARYASSET WHERE ZTITLE = '$ESCAPED_BOOK_TITLE'; \
   DETACH DATABASE real_db;"

echo "✔ Successfully copied \"$BOOK_TITLE\" to fixture."=====
#!/bin/zsh

# Creates a fresh, empty test fixture database with a consistent name and correct schema.
# Usage: ./create_fixture.sh <username>

set -e

FIXTURE_USER=$1
if [[ -z "$FIXTURE_USER" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 <username>"
  exit 1
fi

source "$(dirname "$0")/_common.sh"

# --- Define Paths ---
echo "DEBUG: Searching for real DB in: [$HOME/$BKLIBRARY_USER_SUBPATH]"
REAL_DB_PATH=$(find "$HOME/$BKLIBRARY_USER_SUBPATH" -name "BKLibrary-*.sqlite" | head -n 1)
echo "DEBUG: REAL_DB_PATH resolved to: [$REAL_DB_PATH]"
if [[ ! -f "$REAL_DB_PATH" ]]; then
    echo "Error: Real Apple Books database not found. Find command returned empty."
    exit 1
fi

FIXTURE_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/$BKLIBRARY_FIXTURE_SUBPATH/$FIXTURE_USER/$BKLIBRARY_USER_SUBPATH"
# Use a consistent, predictable name for the fixture database.
FIXTURE_DB_PATH="$FIXTURE_DIR/BKLibrary-fixture.sqlite"

# --- Main Logic ---
echo "Creating new fixture for user: $FIXTURE_USER"

mkdir -p "$FIXTURE_DIR"

# Apple Books domain

This page is the compressed record of what the project learned about Apple Books storage on macOS — the facts BookMinder's code and specs rest on, stated so an agent can write correct code without opening `docs/apple_books.md`. The doc is the territory map from the research spike, with evidence, screenshots, and the discovery narrative; this page points into it by section name only where depth or evidence lives beyond the fact itself. What a spec pins against the fixtures is established; the rest is recorded observation, and what was never established is stated as unknown.

## Data sources

- **B-40 — Two containers, one glob.** Apple Books keeps its data in two sandboxed containers under `~/Library/Containers/`: `com.apple.BKAgentService/Data/Documents/iBooks/Books/` holds `Books.plist` beside the per-book `<asset-id>.epub` files, and `com.apple.iBooksX/Data/Documents/BKLibrary/` holds the library database. The database file name carries per-install numeric segments, so `library.py` discovers it by glob (`BKLibrary-*.sqlite`) and takes the first match — never look it up by literal name; the fixture's `BKLibrary-fixture.sqlite` passes the same glob. Depth: doc, "Container Directories" and "Data Sources".
- **B-41 — Books.plist is the catalogue, the database is the reading state.** Each entry in the plist's `Books` list carries `itemName`, `artistName`, `path` (the only file path the code reads), and `updateDate`; `BKPercentComplete` appears only on finished books and is always 1.0, so the plist cannot express reading progress. Reading state — `ZREADINGPROGRESS` (0.0 to 1.0), `ZLASTOPENDATE`, `ZISFINISHED`, `ZDATEFINISHED`, `ZCREATIONDATE` — lives in the database table `ZBKLIBRARYASSET`, which is also the authoritative catalogue: titles the database knew were missing from the plist even in a fresh snapshot, for a reason never established, so absence from the plist proves nothing about library membership or cloud status. BookMinder cares about the user's relationship to the book, which is why `list recent` and `list all` read the database and only `list_books`/`find_book_by_title` read the plist. Depth: doc, "Data Sources" and "Progress Data Sources Hierarchy".
- **B-42 — `updateDate` means something unknown.** The plist's `updateDate` is probably the publisher's revision date rather than reading activity; that was never verified, and the consequence was a decision: the `sort_by='updated'` feature was deleted as YAGNI because sorting on a field of unknown meaning is not a feature. Recency comes from `ZLASTOPENDATE`.
- **B-43 — Never filter by on-disk file existence.** Books lazy-download from iCloud: a library entry with no `.epub` on disk is a valid, normal entry. Presence on disk is a download state, not a membership test, and no code path stats a book file.
- **B-44 — Apple epoch.** Core Data timestamps in the database count seconds from 2001-01-01 UTC, not 1970; raw values look like plausible Unix times and are silently about 31 years wrong. `library.py` converts with `APPLE_EPOCH + timedelta(seconds=value)`. Conversion detail: doc, "Apple Timestamp Format Details".

## The library table and its columns

- **B-45 — ZSTATE.** A small integer enum on `ZBKLIBRARYASSET`. The mapping the code encodes: 1 = present locally (regular downloaded books and downloaded samples), 3 = cloud book, 6 = cloud sample not yet downloaded; the fixture's cloud rows carry NULL `ZKIND` and `ZPATH`. ZSTATE 5 is unmapped: a `ZSERIESID` join from an owned book returned 5 on the series entity row (title = series name, author "MultipleAuthors") and on unowned member titles sharing the series id, no criterion for telling those apart was established, and the population is large (store collections, public-domain classics). Which values show a cloud icon is unsettled too: cloud-icon books were seen at 1, 3, and 6, but that observation crossed devices (iPhone UI against the Mac's database, where the same title can legitimately differ), so 1 may mean local-on-the-queried-machine. When a census is taken, enumerate all distinct values DB-first and characterize each — never reason UI-first from the values already seen. Depth and evidence: doc, "Observed ZSTATE Mappings" under Domain Language, and "Series Collections".
- **B-46 — Sample detection is a composite predicate.** `is_sample` = `ZSTATE = 6 OR ZISSAMPLE = 1`, and the specs pin both halves (a 6/0 row and a 1/1 row are both samples). `ZISSAMPLE = 0` proves nothing: unmistakable UI samples carried 0 and were identifiable only by ZSTATE 6. The proposed lifecycle — a store sample enters as 6/0 and becomes 1/1 once opened or downloaded — was never observed on one row before and after; it is inferred from one title flipping between queries. Per-title ZSTATE/ZISSAMPLE values are therefore point-in-time: re-run the query, never quote a title from notes. Depth: doc, "Sample Book Handling".
- **B-47 — Cloud display and the cloud filter disagree, by ruling.** `is_cloud` = `ZSTATE in (3, 6)`, so a cloud sample renders with the cloud glyph, but `--filter cloud` on `list recent` matches `ZSTATE = 3` only and `!cloud` matches `ZSTATE != 3` — a cloud sample displays as cloud yet is excluded by the cloud filter. The specs pin only that filtered rows are cloud, not the predicate's width, and the `!cloud` spec holds only because no fixture row sits at ZSTATE 6 with progress.
